newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq shares pushed up at end by Intel.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq shares pushed up at end by Intel.

text.p: Nasdaq shares fought their way back to positive territory on Wednesday after early session losses, drawing strength from Intel Corp, which shrugged off a patent-infringement lawsuit concerns to end higher.

The Nasdaq composite finished up nearly two points or 0.15 percent at 1336, after sinking as low as 1328 during the day. The Dow industrials, which held solid gains throughout the day, retreated at the end to close up about 12 points at 7286.
"Nasdaq was weak early in the day when Intel was down and it came back at the end as Intel rallied," one trader said.
Intel Corp pared early losses which were sparked by news on Tuesday that Digital Equipment Corp filed a patent suit against Intel and would seek a "huge" damage award.

Intel shares closed up 1/2 at 152-7/8 after hitting a session low of 146-1/8. Intel responded to the suit by saying its products did not infringe on Digital's patents and it would vigorously defend itself.
Another trader said the late-day market recovery was partly due to short-covering, and technology shares were mixed.
Nasdaq advancing issues beat declining issues 2291 to 1983 on total volume of about 630 million.
